outcomes: A Node monorepo on npm, pnpm or yarn workspaces, Turborepo and Lerna on those workspaces included, is read as its packages, each a component named by its directory
Each package lists the packages of the same workspace it depends on, so a change to one package names the packages that depend on it
Each package names the lockfile whose diff is its dependency change and the standard places its test and coverage reports are written
The answer is a workspace probe result, so the detector can move to an extension of its own without a contract change
nonGoals: Running npm, pnpm, yarn, turbo or lerna, or reading node_modules
Mapping changed files, tests and coverage to components, finding dependents, and diffing the lockfile: the change analyses own them
Importing an orchestrator's graph export, such as nx graph or turbo ls: the Nx detector and later slices own it
A single package.json without workspaces and bun workspaces
Rush, whose projects rush.json lists: the Rush detector owns it

requirements.text: The members are the directories holding a package.json that match the packages of pnpm-workspace.yaml when it declares them, else the root package.json workspaces, a list or the packages of an object. A pattern takes *, ?, [...], {a,b} and **, and one starting with ! excludes; node_modules, .git and dot-directories no pattern names are skipped. Each member is a component named by its directory, with its package name and version. The root is not a member; a repository declaring no members is not detected.

A member depends on another when one of its dependencies, devDependencies, optionalDependencies or peerDependencies names that member with the workspace: protocol, with file:, link: or portal: to its directory, or with a version range its version satisfies. pnpm counts a range only when linkWorkspacePackages is true in pnpm-workspace.yaml or link-workspace-packages=true in .npmrc. Any other dependency is external and is no edge.

The detector answers a workspace probe request with a probe result the probe protocol accepts: a project per member with its path, package name, package.json, version and dependency paths, attributed to package-json when asked, and its metadata. A request's paths limit the answer to those members. The result watches the root package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml, .npmrc and lockfiles, whether they exist or not.

Each member's metadata names the ecosystem node, the package manager (the packageManager field, else pnpm-workspace.yaml, else the lockfile, else npm), the root lockfile of that manager, else another root lockfile (pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, package-lock.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json), and the report patterns relative to the member: JUnit XML and LCOV, Cobertura, Clover or Istanbul coverage-final.json at their standard places.

A package.json or pnpm-workspace.yaml that cannot be read or parsed, a pattern that is not valid, two members with one package name and a walk that reaches its bound are diagnostics: the member is left out, the first directory keeps the name, or the walk stops, and the detector answers with what it read. It never fails the run.
